**Done**: `company-handbook/SKILL.md`. It has the frontmatter, using your lead's description word for word, and section headings for all seven content areas, ready for pasting. The runbook section has a per-alert template (meaning, severity, steps, escalation) so the 35 entries stay consistent.

Three things to tell your lead. None of them change the one-skill decision:

1. **The skill may rarely load.** Claude decides whether to load a skill mostly from its description. "Anything related to our company" gives no concrete triggers, so a request like "fix this TS lint issue" or "the DiskPressure alert fired" may not match. A description that lists the topics would fix this and is still one line, for example: *"Company handbook: Python/TypeScript style, deploy and rollback for our 4 services, on-call alert runbook, PTO/expense policy, brand voice, org chart, internal glossary. Use when writing code, deploying, handling alerts, drafting marketing copy, or answering policy/people questions."*

2. **All 3,000 lines load every time.** When the skill triggers, the whole SKILL.md goes into context. A lint question would pull in PTO policy and the glossary along with the style rules. Anthropic's guidance is to keep SKILL.md under about 500 lines. The low-effort fix keeps it as one skill: put each section in its own file in the same folder (`runbook.md`, `style.md`, …) and have SKILL.md link to them. Claude then reads only the file it needs. That's roughly 10 minutes more work.

3. **Phone numbers go wherever the skill goes.** The org chart's personal contact info will be loaded into any session that triggers the skill and will travel wherever the skill is shared. You may want to leave the phone numbers out or link to the HR system instead.

I can make #1 or #2 now if you want. Otherwise, the file is ready as written.
